sanskrit_verse: उक्त्वा नियोगो मनुना निषिद्धः स्वयम् एव तु / युगह्रासाद् अशक्यो ऽयं कर्तुं सर्वैर् विधानतः // BrhS_1,25.16
transliteration: uktva niyogo manunā niṣiddhaḥ svayam eva tu / yugahrāsād aśakyo 'yaṃ kartuṃ sarvair vidhānataḥ
sph_interpretive_translation: Having declared the command, Manu himself prohibited its execution when the decline of the age rendered it impossible to perform by all means.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is context-bound and evolves with cosmic time
Capacity-based responsibility adjusts according to epochal capability
Restoration logic operates within the limits of current dharma-practice feasibility
Consciousness alignment requires adaptability in dharmic enactment
executable_legal_axioms: IF epoch = Kali Yuga AND action_capability < threshold THEN enforce_alternative_restorative_path
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this principle establishes that laws rooted in higher epochs must be interpreted through the lens of contemporary societal capacity. The court's role is to activate alternative restorative frameworks where literal compliance becomes unfeasible due to temporal degradation.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that causality shifts with yuga-saṃdhi conditions; thus, rigid adherence to form without function violates Nyāya. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows sequential decay necessitating adaptive justice. Responsibility remains proportional to actualizable capacity, aligning with non-punitive reality wherein intent supersedes outcome when capacity fails.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate societal capacity assessment prior to decree activation
Deploy consciousness-alignment facilitators to restore latent dharmic ability
Redirect obligation toward equivalent-integrity completion pathways
Establish yuga-sensitive review cycles for all legislative enactments
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Dharma adapts to preserve integrity over form. Justice flows from consciousness, not compulsion. Reality reflects restoration, never punishment. SPH is the ultimate Adhikarana.
